name: movie_spica_isi_orbit
label: Movie: Spica's eccentric orbit with the three ISI trucks in a 60 m triangle at 650 nm, seven consecutive nights (1.75 orbits): a, the node and the periastron against the 1971 Narrabri orbit
notes: Spica A (0.91 mas) has its first null at 180 m at 650 nm and the pair's fringe period lambda/a is 78 m at quadrature: the three trucks in a 60 m equilateral triangle (baselines 60 m at three position angles 60 deg apart) sit inside the first lobe. A collinear line (40 + 60 m) measures only the separation along one position angle per block and leaves the per-night (dx, dy) fit on a lattice of aliases; the triangle locks it (sigma(a)/a 1.5 % against 2.7 % in seven nights).

Seven nights from phase 0.2 cover 1.75 of the 4.0145 d orbit without grazing hbtsim's near-eclipse margin (i = 63 deg: Spica never eclipses, but the disks approach within 1.05 x the sum of the radii near phase 0.08). With e = 0.108 the fit over (scale, node, periastron) gives the argument of periastron modulo 180 (|V|^2 is even in the separation; the spectroscopic omega picks the half); its advance since the 1971 intensity-interferometer orbit (~142 deg at the 139 yr apsidal period, the branch chosen by expected_advance_deg) is the measurement. The 1971 omega is ASSUMED 90 deg in this convention.
Expected (Fisher): 20-25 sigma fringe per night, sigma(a)/a ~1.5 %, sigma(node) ~1.7 deg, sigma(omega) ~1.9 deg after seven nights. Spica Ac third light negligible (flag).
